paper_1_medical_nlp.pdf.title: Attention-Based Deep Learning for Medical Document Intelligence

objective.value: To design an attention-only neural architecture capable of capturing subtle diagnostic clues without requiring prohibitive recurrent computations.
objective.evidence_quote: Our objective in this research is to design an attention-only neural architecture capable of capturing subtle diagnostic clues without requiring prohibitive recurrent computations.

abstract.value: Automated understanding of clinical and medical documents requires high-precision semantic parsing. In this paper, we introduce MedLens-Transformer, a specialized multi-head self-attention architecture tailored for clinical documentation analysis. Our model processes long-range dependencies across complex EHR records and unstructured clinical narratives. Evaluated on the newly released PubMedMedDoc-50k benchmark, MedLens-Transformer establishes a new state-of-the-art with 94.2% classification accuracy and 93.8% Macro-F1 score.
abstract.evidence_quote: Automated understanding of clinical and medical documents requires high-precision semantic parsing. In this paper, we introduce MedLens-Transformer, a specialized multi-head self-attention architecture tailored for clinical documentation analysis. Our model processes long-range dependencies across complex EHR records and unstructured clinical narratives. Evaluated on the newly released PubMedMedDoc-50k benchmark, MedLens-Transformer establishes a new state-of-the-art with 94.2% classification accuracy and 93.8% Macro-F1 score.

methodology.value: MedLens-Transformer consists of a 12-layer bidirectional encoder with 768 hidden dimensions and 12 attention heads using scaled dot-product attention with specialized relative positional encodings and token embeddings augmented with biomedical entity type indicators extracted using UMLS concept mapping.
methodology.evidence_quote: The MedLens-Transformer consists of a 12-layer bidirectional encoder with 768 hidden dimensions and 12 attention heads. We employ scaled dot-product attention with specialized relative positional encodings designed for hierarchical document structures. Token embeddings are augmented with biomedical entity type indicators extracted using UMLS concept mapping.

datasets.value: PubMedMedDoc-50k benchmark, comprising 50,000 annotated clinical discharge summaries categorized into 25 diagnostic specialties, partitioned into 80% training, 10% validation, and 10% test splits.
datasets.evidence_quote: Our experimental evaluation leverages the PubMedMedDoc-50k benchmark, comprising 50,000 annotated clinical discharge summaries categorized into 25 diagnostic specialties. Data was partitioned into 80% training, 10% validation, and 10% test splits.

algorithms.value: MedLens-Transformer, AdamW optimizer, and cross-entropy loss with label smoothing.
algorithms.evidence_quote: We deploy the AdamW optimizer with a learning rate of 2e-5, linear warmup over the first 10% of training steps, and cosine learning rate decay. Cross-entropy loss with label smoothing (epsilon = 0.1) is utilized to prevent overconfidence.

metrics.evidence_quote: Specifically, MedLens-Transformer achieved an accuracy of 94.2% and a Macro-F1 score of 93.8%, exceeding ClinicalBERT by 3.4 percentage points.

results.value: MedLens-Transformer achieved an accuracy of 94.2% and a Macro-F1 score of 93.8% on the test partition of PubMedMedDoc-50k, exceeding ClinicalBERT by 3.4 percentage points.
results.evidence_quote: Specifically, MedLens-Transformer achieved an accuracy of 94.2% and a Macro-F1 score of 93.8%, exceeding ClinicalBERT by 3.4 percentage points.

limitations.value: Evaluation is restricted to English medical summaries, tested only on 5,000 samples due to computational resource constraints, and the tokenization vocabulary does not fully cover handwritten clinician annotations.
limitations.evidence_quote: Our evaluation is restricted to English medical summaries and was tested only on 5,000 samples due to computational resource constraints. Furthermore, our tokenization vocabulary does not fully cover handwritten clinician annotations.

future_work.value: Extend the architecture to multilingual clinical notes and evaluate self-supervised pre-training across multi-modal records.
future_work.evidence_quote: Future work will extend the architecture to multilingual clinical notes and evaluate self-supervised pre-training across multi-modal records.

paper_3_hybrid_ir.pdf.title: Hybrid Information Retrieval for Scientific Document Search

objective.value: Demonstrate that reciprocal rank fusion yields superior retrieval robustness across heterogeneous scientific disciplines by balancing exact lexical matching and semantic generalization.
objective.evidence_quote: Our objective is to demonstrate that reciprocal rank fusion yields superior retrieval robustness across heterogeneous scientific disciplines.

abstract.value: Modern academic search requires balancing exact lexical matching of technical terms with semantic generalization. We introduce HybridLens, combining Okapi BM25 and dense bi-encoder embeddings via Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) coupled with a Cross-Encoder reranker. Evaluated on MS-MARCO-Academic, HybridLens achieves nDCG@10 of 0.642 and MRR@10 of 0.681.

We introduce HybridLens, combining Okapi BM25 and dense bi-encoder embeddings via Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) coupled with a Cross-Encoder reranker. Evaluated on MS-MARCO-Academic, HybridLens achieves nDCG@10 of 0.642 and MRR@10 of 0.681.

methodology.value: HybridLens fuses sparse scores from BM25 with dense inner product scores from BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) with constant k=60, after which top-20 candidates are reranked by an ms-marco-MiniLM cross-encoder.

objective.value: To accurately forecast prospective citation ties between papers using structural and content features.
objective.evidence_quote: Our objective is to accurately forecast prospective citation ties between papers using structural and content features.

abstract.value: Predicting missing citation links in scientific bibliographies is vital for tracking literature trends. In this study, we propose CiteGraph-GNN, an inductive relational graph attention network capable of capturing multi-hop topological neighborhoods alongside document title semantics. Tested on the standard Cora-Citation-Graph benchmark, CiteGraph-GNN achieves an MRR of 0.784 and Hit@10 of 86.5%.

2024.emnlp-industry.13-paper-1.pdf.title: PDFTriage:  Question Answering over Long, Structured Documents

objective.value: To propose PDFTriage, an approach that enables models to retrieve context from structured documents based on either structure or content, thereby overcoming the limitations of existing retrieval-augmented LLMs that represent structured documents as plain text.
objective.evidence_quote: To bridge this fundamental gap in handling structured documents, we propose an approach called PDFTriage that enables models to retrieve the context based on either structure or content.

abstract.value: Large Language Models (LLMs) struggle with document question answering (QA) when documents exceed their context length. While existing works retrieve context by representing documents as plain text, this is incongruous with the rich structure of PDFs, web pages, and presentations (e.g., pages, tables, sections). To bridge this gap, the authors propose PDFTriage, allowing models to retrieve context based on structure or content, and release a benchmark dataset of 900+ human-generated questions over 80 structured documents across 10 categories.
abstract.evidence_quote: Large Language Models (LLMs) have issues with document question answering (QA) in situations where the document is unable to fit in the small context length of an LLM.

methodology.value: PDFTriage leverages the structure of PDFs and the interactive system functions capability of GPT-3.5 to extract answers more precisely and accurately. It performs multi-stage querying of the document, retrieving and adding context as needed for different document QA tasks.
methodology.evidence_quote: This strategy leverages the structure of PDFs and the interactive system functions capability of GPT-3.5 to extract answers more precisely and accurately than existing naive approaches.

datasets.value: A benchmark dataset consisting of human-generated questions over structured documents from 10 different categories of question types, containing 908 questions across 82 documents, with an average document containing 4,257 tokens of text.
datasets.evidence_quote: In total, our dataset consists of 908 questions across 82 documents. On average a document contains 4,257 tokens of text, connected to headers, subheaders, section paragraphs, captions, and more.

algorithms.value: GPT-3.5 utilizing text-embedding-ada-002 embeddings for page retrieval and chunk retrieval baselines, along with the proposed PDFTriage approach.
algorithms.evidence_quote: For our first baseline, we index the pages of each individual document using text-embedding-ada-002 embeddings.

metrics.value: Readability, Informativeness, Clarity, Accuracy, Overall Quality, and Cohen's kappa score for annotator agreement.
metrics.evidence_quote: In our annotation study, we also asked the annotators to score PDFTriage, Page Retrieval, and Chunk Retrieval answers across five major qualities: accuracy, informativeness, readability/understandability, and clarity.

results.value: Annotators favored the PDFTriage answer over half of the time (50.7%). PDFTriage scored higher than Page Retrieval and Chunk Retrieval across readability (4.2 vs 4.1, 4.1), informativeness (3.9 vs 3.7, 3.4), accuracy (3.8 vs 3.6, 3.4), and overall quality (3.9 vs 3.8, 3.6), while achieving an average Cohen's kappa score of 0.584 for annotator agreement.
results.evidence_quote: In Figure 3, we found that annotators favored the PDFTriage answer over half of the time (50.7%) and favored the Chunk Retrieval approach over the Page Retrieval approach.

objective.value: To develop a comprehensive RAG-based question-answering system capable of answering complex, multifaceted questions that necessitate the integration, retrieval, and interpretation of diverse data types found within PDF documents, including text, images, vector diagrams, graphs, and tables.
objective.evidence_quote: Our objective is to address this gap by developing a comprehensive system capable of answering complex, multifaceted questions that necessitate the integration and interpretation of diverse data types.

abstract.value: This paper presents an advancement in Question-Answering (QA) systems using a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) framework to enhance information extraction from PDF files. Recognizing the richness and diversity of data within PDFs—including text, images, vector diagrams, graphs, and tables—poses unique challenges for existing QA systems primarily designed for textual content. We seek to develop a comprehensive RAG-based QA system that will effectively address complex multi-modal questions, where several data types are put together in the question. This is mainly achieved by refining approaches toward processing and integrating non-textual elements in PDFs into the RAG framework to derive precise and relevant answers, as well as finetuning large language models to adapt better into our system. We provide an in-depth experimental evaluation of our system, demonstrating its capabilities to extract accurate information that can be adapted to different types of content across PDFs. This work not only pushes the boundaries of retrieval-augmented QA systems but also lays a foundation for further research in multimodal data integration and processing.
abstract.evidence_quote: This paper presents an advancement in Question-Answering (QA) systems using a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) framework to enhance information extraction from PDF files.

methodology.value: The proposed PDF Integrated Enhanced Retrieval Question Answering (PIER-QA) system consists of three main components: (1) PDF Preprocessing, where headers and footers are removed using DBSCAN clustering, converted to markdown using Marker, image captions are generated, and tables are compressed into a dictionary format; (2) Embedding and Storage, where text chunks of 1000 characters are embedded via GTE-large, stored in ElasticSearch, and indexed/clustered using RAPTOR; and (3) Question Answering, which embeds queries, retrieves top-10 chunks, and uses a RAG-aware finetuned LLM to generate answers with image/table recovery capabilities.
methodology.evidence_quote: We propose PDF Integrated Enhanced Retrieval Question Answering (PIER-QA) system consisting of three main components as shown in Figure 1.

datasets.value: A dataset consisting of 8 private internal documents from a production company, where 6 documents were used for fine-tuning and the remaining documents were used for testing, yielding a test set of 100 question-answer pairs generated by manually prompting GPT-4o.
datasets.evidence_quote: Our dataset consists of 8 private internal documents from a production company. We used 6 of them for finetuning our model as described in Section 3, leaving the rest for testing.

algorithms.value: DBSCAN clustering algorithm, Marker (machine-learning-based tool for markdown conversion), GTE-large embedding model, ElasticSearch, RAPTOR, LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation), and Llama3-70B-Instruct / RAG-Llama3-70B.
algorithms.evidence_quote: Headers and footers are removed using DBSCAN clustering algorithm Fahim [2022] which improves accuracy... embedded by GTE-large Li et al. [2023] and stored using ElasticSearch Kathare et al. [2020] for efficient retrieval. RAPTOR Sarthi et al. [2024] is used... We finetune Llama3-70B-Instruct Grattafiori et al. [2024] with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA)

metrics.value: Similarity (assessed using embeddings from the GTE-large model) and accuracy at different thresholds (accuracy@0.85, accuracy@0.9, and accuracy@0.95), alongside specific image and table retrieval accuracy.
metrics.evidence_quote: Similarity between the generated answers and the gold standard answers was assessed using embeddings from the GTE-large model. Additionally, we used accuracy at different thresholds - accuracy@0.85, accuracy@0.9 and accuracy@0.95 to evaluate the precision of the system.

results.value: PIER-QA achieved higher similarity scores and accuracy across all thresholds (0.85, 0.9, and 0.95) compared to the baseline system. Specifically, with GPT-4o, PIER-QA achieved a similarity score of 0.8837, accuracy@0.85 of 0.7191, accuracy@0.9 of 0.4944, and accuracy@0.95 of 0.1910. The RAG-Llama3-70B model achieved a similarity score of 0.8771, accuracy@0.85 of 0.7303, accuracy@0.9 of 0.4719, and accuracy@0.95 of 0.2135. For non-textual retrieval tasks, PIER-QA achieved 65.66% accuracy for image retrieval and 48.38% accuracy for table retrieval.
results.evidence_quote: In Table 3, our PIER-QA system achieved considerable accuracies for image and table retrieval, at 65.66% and 48.38%, respectively.

limitations.value: The DBSCAN clustering algorithm might not always differentiate headers, footers, and main content in highly variable PDF formats, potentially causing a loss of essential information. Markdown conversion tools may fail on complex tables, leading to formatting errors or information loss. Additionally, the system always performs retrieval for every query, leading to potentially unnecessary retrieval steps and latency overhead.
limitations.evidence_quote: DBSCAN clustering algorithm might not always differentiate headers, footers and the main content, especially in highly variable PDF document formats. This misidentification could lead to loss of essential information in the further processing.

future_work.value: Research work shall be incorporated in the future to overcome the mentioned limitations with advanced tools and technologies.
future_work.evidence_quote: Research work shall be incorporated in the future to overcome the mentioned limitations with advanced tools and technologies.

research paper-3.pdf.title: NeuSym-RAG: Hybrid Neural Symbolic Retrieval with Multiview Structuring for PDF Question Answering

objective.value: To propose NeuSym-RAG, a hybrid neural-symbolic retrieval framework for semi-structured PDF-based question answering that combines neural and symbolic paradigms in an interactive process using multi-view chunking and schema-based parsing.
objective.evidence_quote: In this work, we propose NeuSym-RAG, a hybrid neural symbolic retrieval framework which combines both paradigms in an interactive process.

abstract.value: The increasing number of academic papers poses significant challenges for researchers to efficiently acquire key details. While retrieval augmented generation (RAG) shows great promise in large language model (LLM) based automated question answering, previous works often isolate neural and symbolic retrieval despite their complementary strengths. Moreover, conventional single-view chunking neglects the rich structure and layout of PDFs, e.g., sections and tables. In this work, we propose NeuSym-RAG, a hybrid neural symbolic retrieval framework which combines both paradigms in an interactive process. By leveraging multi-view chunking and schema-based parsing, NeuSym-RAG organizes semi-structured PDF content into both the relational database and vectorstore, enabling LLM agents to iteratively gather context until sufficient to generate answers. Experiments on three full PDF-based QA datasets, including a self-annotated one AIRQA-REAL, show that NeuSym-RAG stably defeats both the vector-based RAG and various structured baselines, highlighting its capacity to unify both retrieval schemes and utilize multiple views.
abstract.evidence_quote: The increasing number of academic papers poses significant challenges for researchers to efficiently acquire key details. ... Experiments on three full PDF-based QA datasets, including a self-annotated one AIRQA-REAL, show that NeuSym-RAG stably defeats both the vector-based RAG and various structured baselines, highlighting its capacity to unify both retrieval schemes and utilize multiple views.

methodology.value: A hybrid neural-symbolic retrieval framework combining multi-view chunking and schema-based parsing to organize semi-structured PDF content into relational databases and vectorstores, allowing LLM agents to iteratively gather context through multi-turn interactions.
methodology.evidence_quote: By leveraging multi-view chunking and schema-based parsing, NeuSym-RAG organizes semi-structured PDF content into both the relational database and vectorstore, enabling LLM agents to iteratively gather context until sufficient to generate answers.

datasets.value: AIRQA-REAL (self-annotated dataset with 553 questions from AI papers in 2023 and 2024), M3SciQA (452 test samples), and SciDQA (2937 test samples).
datasets.evidence_quote: Experiments on three full PDF-based QA datasets, including a self-annotated one AIRQA-REAL, show that NeuSym-RAG stably defeats both the vector-based RAG and various structured baselines... To validate the universality, we also convert two other full-PDF-based Q&A datasets, namely M3SciQA and SciDQA.

algorithms.value: Large language models and vision-language models including GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4-1106-vision-preview, InternLM2.5, Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-VL-72B-Instruct, and DeepSeek-R1, along with tools like PyMuPDF and MinerU.
algorithms.evidence_quote: For closed-source ones, we use GPT-4o-mini-2024-07-18 and GPT-4-1106-vision-preview. Regarding state-of-the-art open-source LLMs, we include InternLM2.5, Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-VL-72B-Instruct, and DeepSeek-R1.

metrics.value: Python-style answer formatting and instance-specific, execution-based evaluation using 18 subjective or objective functions with optional parameters.
metrics.evidence_quote: Specifically, we 1) adopt answer formatting similar to DABench, which imposes Python-style restrictions on output..., and 2) implement instance-specific, execution-based evaluation by designing 18 functions with optional parameters.

results.value: NeuSym-RAG remarkably outperforms the Classic RAG baseline across all datasets, achieving a minimal 17.3% improvement on AIRQA-REAL for all LLMs, and Qwen2.5-VL-72B-Instruct elevates overall accuracy by 29.1% compared to Classic RAG.
results.evidence_quote: NeuSym-RAG remarkably outperforms the Classic RAG baseline across all datasets, with a minimal 17.3% improvement on AIRQA-REAL for all LLMs... NeuSym-RAG with Qwen2.5-VL-72B-Instruct elevates the overall accuracy by 29.1%, compared to the Classic RAG baseline.

limitations.value: 1) The pipeline of parsing and encoding PDF content is relatively slow due to the need for higher-capacity OCR models. 2) The iterative chain-of-retrieval procedure incurs extra time delay compared to classic RAG. 3) NeuSym-RAG requires external documents to exhibit implicit structures or layouts. 4) AIRQA-REAL is currently limited to the domain of AI research papers.
limitations.evidence_quote: Despite the superiority of the proposed NeuSym-RAG framework, it still has the following limitations: 1) The pipeline of parsing and encoding the PDF content is relatively slow... 2) The iterative chain-of-retrieval procedure incurs extra time delay... 3) NeuSym-RAG requires that the external documents exhibit implicit structures or layouts... 4) Currently, AIRQA-REAL are limited to the domain of AI research papers.

future_work.value: 1) Training a specialized LLM agent of medium size to further improve performances and efficiency. 2) Extending Q&A tasks to other vertical domains such as healthcare and law which heavily rely on external well-structured PDF files.
future_work.evidence_quote: Future works include: 1) training a specialized LLM agent of medium size to further improve performances and efficiency, and 2) extending Q&A tasks to other vertical domains such as healthcare and law which heavily rely on external well-structured PDF files.

objective.value: To propose Doc-React, an adaptive iterative framework for answering questions over multi-page, multimodal documents by balancing information gain and uncertainty reduction at each step.
objective.evidence_quote: Inspired by iterative frameworks like ReAct, which refine retrieval through feedback, we propose Doc-React, an adaptive iterative framework that balances information gain and uncertainty reduction at each step.

abstract.value: Answering questions over multi-page, multimodal documents, including text and figures, is a critical challenge for applications that require answers to integrate information across multiple modalities and contextual dependencies. Existing methods, such as single-turn retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), struggle to retrieve fine-grained and contextually relevant information from large, heterogeneous documents, leading to suboptimal performance. Inspired by iterative frameworks like ReAct, which refine retrieval through feedback, we propose Doc-React, an adaptive iterative framework that balances information gain and uncertainty reduction at each step. Doc-React leverages InfoNCE-guided retrieval to approximate mutual information, enabling dynamic sub-query generation and refinement. A large language model (LLM) serves as both a judge and generator, providing structured feedback to iteratively improve retrieval. By combining mutual information optimization with entropy-aware selection, Doc-React systematically captures relevant multimodal content, achieving strong performance on complex QA tasks.
abstract.evidence_quote: Answering questions over multi-page, multimodal documents, including text and figures, is a critical challenge for applications that require answers to integrate information across multiple modalities and contextual dependencies.

methodology.value: Doc-React uses an adaptive iterative framework with InfoNCE-guided retrieval to approximate mutual information, dynamic sub-query generation via an LLM acting as a judge and generator, and step-wise normalized information gain optimization combined with entropy-aware selection.
methodology.evidence_quote: Doc-React leverages InfoNCE-guided retrieval to approximate mutual information, enabling dynamic sub-query generation and refinement. A large language model (LLM) serves as both a judge and generator, providing structured feedback to iteratively improve retrieval.

datasets.value: SlideVQA and VisualWebBench (along with MMLongBench in experiments).
datasets.evidence_quote: To evaluate baselines and DocReact on multi-page document question-answering, we apply our method on two datasets, SlideVQA (Tanaka et al., 2023) and VisualWebBench (Liu et al., 2024b).

algorithms.value: GPT-4o, InternVL, MiniCPM, ColPali, and VisRAG-Ret as baselines and retriever backbones.
algorithms.evidence_quote: For our comparison experiments, we use two lines of baselines, including Multi-image MLLMs: GPT4-o, InternVL (Chen et al., 2024), and MiniCPM (Yao et al., 2024)... and Multimodal RAG: ColPali (Faysse et al., 2024) and VisRAG-Ret (Yu et al., 2024).

metrics.evidence_quote: Dataset MMLongBench SlideVQA Method Model F1 Acc F1 Acc

results.value: DocReact with GPT-4o achieves F1 of 38.07 and Accuracy of 38.29 on MMLongBench, and F1 of 54.87 and Accuracy of 55.04 on SlideVQA, outperforming multimodal RAG and multi-image MLLM baselines.

research paper-5.pdf.title: MHier-RAG: Multi-Modal RAG for Visual-Rich Document Question-Answering via Hierarchical and Multi-Granularity Reasoning

objective.value: To propose a novel multi-modal RAG model, named MHier-RAG, that leverages both textual and visual information across long-range pages to facilitate accurate question answering for visual-rich documents by addressing inter-modal disconnection and cross-page fragmentation.
objective.evidence_quote: To address these challenges, a novel multi-modal RAG model, named MHier-RAG, was proposed, leveraging both textual and visual information across long-range pages to facilitate accurate question answering for visual-rich documents.

abstract.value: The multi-modal long-context document question-answering task aims to locate and integrate multi-modal evidences distributed across multiple pages. Existing methods suffer from hallucinations or inter-modal disconnection and cross-page fragmentation. MHier-RAG introduces a hierarchical indexing method with flattened in-page chunks and topological cross-page chunks, combined with a multi-granularity semantic retrieval method using joint similarity evaluation and LLM-based re-ranking.
abstract.evidence_quote: The multi-modal long-context document question-answering task aims to locate and integrate multi-modal evidences (such as texts, tables, charts, images, and layouts) distributed across multiple pages, for question understanding and answer generation.

methodology.value: MHier-RAG uses a hierarchical indexing method combining flattened in-page chunks (for in-page multi-modal associations) and topological cross-page chunks (for long-distance cross-page dependencies), alongside a multi-granularity semantic retrieval method involving page-level parent page retrieval with LLM-based re-ranking and document-level summary retrieval, followed by CoT prompting with a structured output format for answer generation.
methodology.evidence_quote: A hierarchical indexing method with the integration of flattened in-page chunks and topological cross-page chunks was designed to jointly establish in-page multi-modal associations and long-distance cross-page dependencies.

datasets.value: MMLongBench-Doc comprises 135 long PDF documents averaging 47.5 pages and 21,214 tokens with 1,082 expert-annotated questions. LongDocURL comprises 396 long PDF documents averaging 85.6 pages and 43,622.6 tokens with 2,325 question-answer pairs.
datasets.evidence_quote: MMLongBench-Doc (Ma et al. 2024b) comprises 135 long PDF documents, each containing an average of 47.5 pages and 21,214 tokens. It consists of 1,082 expert-annotated questions. LongDocURL (Deng et al. 2025) is constructed upon 396 long PDF documents, with an average length of 85.6 pages and 43,622.6 tokens. It collects 2,325 high-quality question-answer pairs.

algorithms.value: Docling for PDF parsing, off-the-shelf Language Models (LLMs) and Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) for encoding and answer generation, along with ColBERTv2, M3DocRAG, QWen-Plus, DeepSeek-V2, Claude-3 Opus, Gemini-1.5-Pro, GPT-4o, DeepSeek-VL, InternLM-XC2-4KHD, mPLUG-DocOwl 1.5, Qwen-VL, and GPT-4V used as baselines or components.
algorithms.evidence_quote: Docling (Livathinos et al. 2025) was used for pdf parsing. The off-the-shelf LLMs/LVLMs were utilized for answer generation.

metrics.value: Accuracy of distinct evidence modality types, evidence pages, generalized accuracy, and F1 score.
metrics.evidence_quote: We reported the accuracy of distinct evidence modality types and evidence pages. The generalized accuracy and F1 score were also recorded.

results.value: On MMLongBench-Doc, MHier-RAG achieved up to 45.9% accuracy and 34.4% F1 score (with page=10). On LongDocURL, MHier-RAG achieved 57.2% accuracy (with page=10), outperforming SOTA M3DocRAG by a margin of 5% in generalized accuracy.
results.evidence_quote: MHier-RAG method surpassed the current SOTA M3DocRAG by a margin of 5% in terms of generalized accuracy, when the page number was set to ten.

limitations.value: Overly broad retrieval may introduce distractors in unanswerable cases.
limitations.evidence_quote: It is worth noting that, the accuracy of unanswerable questions (UNA) in four variant models increased, suggesting that overly broad retrieval may introduce distractors in unanswerable cases.
